import json, os, sys
base = sys.argv[1]
def load(i):
    with open(os.path.join(base, 'drafts', i + '.json')) as f:
        return json.load(f)
def save(i, d):
    with open(os.path.join(base, 'verified', i + '.json'), 'w') as f:
        json.dump(d, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write('\n')

inputs = json.load(open(os.path.join(base, 'inputs.json')))
items = inputs if isinstance(inputs, list) else inputs.get('items', inputs)
src = {x['id']: x['sourceFile'] for x in items if isinstance(x, dict) and 'id' in x}

out = {}

d = load('Q73')
d['verification'] = {"status": "VERIFIED", "changes": [],
  "residualConcerns": "", "spotCheckPriority": "normal"}
out['Q73'] = d

d = load('Q74')
d['verification'] = {"status": "VERIFIED", "changes": [],
  "residualConcerns": "", "spotCheckPriority": "normal"}
out['Q74'] = d

d = load('Q75')
d['exclusionReason'] = "(b) Law review student comment (Jeffrey S. Moorad Sports Law Journal, 2025) arguing a legal and policy position on malpractice liability for NFL team physicians. It has no original methods and no structured review of health evidence; it also offers no athlete health or performance evidence."
d['verification'] = {"status": "CORRECTED",
  "changes": ["exclusionReason: coded (c) not relevant -> (b) opinion piece without methods; the text calls itself a Comment ('This Comment is brought to you') and the topic, NFL players' medical care, is athlete-health adjacent, so (b) fits better. Decision unchanged."],
  "residualConcerns": "", "spotCheckPriority": "normal"}
out['Q75'] = d

d = load('Q76')
d['verification'] = {"status": "VERIFIED", "changes": [],
  "residualConcerns": "Article type is a Sports Medicine 'Current Opinion'. It was kept as INCLUDE (Narrative Review) because it reports a non-systematic screen of 36 RCTs and a worked re-analysis, but a reviewer may judge it an opinion piece under rule (b).",
  "spotCheckPriority": "high"}
out['Q76'] = d

d = load('Q77')
d['paper']['tldr'] = "In recreationally active men, a high-volume start followed by low volume, or steadily rising volume, increased hamstring fascicle length and eccentric strength over 6 weeks. Weekly low volume (48 total reps) increased strength but not fascicle length, and 8 reps every second week (24 total) changed neither."
d['verification'] = {"status": "CORRECTED",
  "changes": ["paper.tldr: said low volume of 24 or 48 total reps increased strength -> only the 48-rep weekly group increased strength; the 24-rep fortnightly group did not ('as few as 48 repetitions in 6 weeks did increase strength'; group 1 'no change (-1%) in strength')."],
  "residualConcerns": "", "spotCheckPriority": "normal"}
out['Q77'] = d

d = load('Q78')
d['evidenceSummary'] = "A PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 NHE training studies (searched in SPORTDiscus, Ovid and PubMed) that measured eccentric strength or biceps femoris architecture after at least 4 weeks. Individual-study pre-post effects after 6 or more weeks were large to very large for eccentric strength at both high and low volumes (abstract: g = 2.12 and 2.28) and very large for fascicle length (g of 2.58 or more), with pennation angle falling by a large to very large amount (g of 1.31 or more). No trend by volume was found, but volumes were not compared statistically."
d['paper']['methods'] = "PRISMA-guided search of three databases (293 records) to 1 December 2018; 13 studies with at least 4 weeks of NHE, pre-post means and SDs, and biceps femoris architecture data were included. Study quality was rated with TESTEX, risk of bias with the Cochrane tool for the RCTs and publication bias with a Rosenthal fail-safe N; Hedges' g values were calculated within studies and a random-effects model estimated between-study effects."
d['paper']['findings'] = "After 6 or more weeks, both high and low volume protocols produced large to very large within-study gains in eccentric strength, and three fascicle length measures showed very large gains (g of 2.58 or more). Weekly volumes ranged from about 21 to 73 repetitions with no clear volume trend. Studies of 4 weeks showed trivial to small change, and control groups showed trivial or negative change (g of 0.14 or less)."
d['paper']['limitations'] = "Only 13 studies, two without a control group; several studies had low TESTEX scores and did not report compliance or blinded assessment; the review was not pre-registered; the volume conclusion rests on uncontrolled pre-post effects. The abstract gives g = 2.12 (high volume) and g = 2.28 (low volume) for strength, but the results attribute g = 2.12 to a single study of eccentric peak torque and do not report g = 2.28."
d['verification'] = {"status": "CORRECTED",
  "changes": [
   "evidenceSummary: called g = 2.12 and 2.28 'pooled' effects -> individual-study pre-post effects as reported in the abstract; results say 'Only one study which assessed eccentric peak torque showed very large increases (g = 2.12)'.",
   "paper.findings: attached the strength g values to fascicle length as well -> strength and fascicle length effects reported separately per results.",
   "paper.methods: omitted fail-safe N and the search end date -> added ('fail-safe N using the Rosenthal method'; 'restricted to 1 December 2018').",
   "paper.limitations: added the abstract versus results conflict on g = 2.28."],
  "residualConcerns": "The abstract's g = 2.28 for low-volume strength does not appear in the results text; check the forest plots (Fig. 3 and 4) if the value matters.",
  "spotCheckPriority": "high"}
out['Q78'] = d

d = load('Q79')
d['paper']['tldr'] = "Sled sprint training improved early acceleration in recreationally active and trained athletes, but it was no better than the same sprinting without a sled, and maximum-velocity sprint time did not improve significantly. The authors recommend 6 or more weeks at 2 to 3 sessions a week."
d['paper']['findings'] = "Pre-post sprint time improved in the acceleration phase (ES 0.61, P = .0001; heterogeneity I2 = 28%) and full sprint (ES 0.36, P = .009), but not in the maximum-velocity phase (ES 0.27, P = .25). Studies with control groups showed no significant RST-versus-control difference in any phase (acceleration ES 0.09, P = .64). Acceleration effects were moderate in recreationally active (ES 0.75) and trained (ES 0.84) participants but small and non-significant in highly trained ones (ES 0.30) and in female samples (ES 0.14); loads below and above 20% of body mass gave similar effects (0.61 vs 0.63), though the higher-load effect was not significant."
d['paper']['athleteDev'] = "For early acceleration in soccer or rugby, a 6-week sled block at 2 to 3 sessions a week improved sprint times in the pooled studies, though unresisted sprinting did about as well. For top speed the review found no significant effect, and the authors suggest that vertical-force methods such as plyometrics may be needed."
d['verification'] = {"status": "CORRECTED",
  "changes": [
   "paper.tldr: 'does not improve top speed' and prescription stated as a finding -> non-significant maximum-velocity change, prescription attributed to the authors (ES 0.27, p = 0.25).",
   "paper.findings: added non-significant female (ES 0.14) and high-load subgroups ('non-significant improvements were found for female sex (ES 0.14)'; 'higher loads (>= 20% BM; ES 0.63)').",
   "paper.athleteDev: added that RST did not beat unresisted sprinting and sourced the vertical-force suggestion ('Perhaps plyometric training')."],
  "residualConcerns": "", "spotCheckPriority": "normal"}
out['Q79'] = d

d = load('Q80')
d['screeningLimitations'] = "Ten players per group, six weeks only, no control group, and usual soccer training and pre-existing training experience were not controlled. The between-group test for eccentric strength was not significant, so a flywheel advantage is not established even though the within-group gain was."
d['paper']['methods'] = "Random allocation to flywheel RDL (inertial load set by a power test; 4 sets of 6 with two extra submaximal pre-repetitions) or traditional RDL (80% of predicted 1RM), twice weekly for 6 weeks with matched set-RPE 8. Outcomes were 3RM RDL and peak eccentric force during the NHE on a Hamstring Solo device before and after training, analysed with a 2 x 2 group x time repeated-measures ANOVA."
d['paper']['limitations'] = "No control group, six weeks only, small groups, and usual training was not controlled. The abstract and discussion describe superior eccentric gains for flywheel, but the interaction test was not significant (P = .18). The text effect sizes (g = 0.18, 0.51, 0.99 and 1.07) also differ slightly from Table 2 (0.2, 0.53, 1.0 and 1.11)."
d['verification'] = {"status": "CORRECTED",
  "changes": [
   "paper.methods: eccentric strength device given as Nordbord -> Hamstring Solo ('positioned on a Hamstring Solo (Hamstring Solo Elite, Kilkenny, Ireland) device').",
   "screeningLimitations: 'no matched training history' -> pre-existing training experience not controlled; all had at least 12 months of resistance training ('athletes' pre-existing training experience ... may have contributed').",
   "paper.limitations: listed all four text versus Table 2 effect size differences."],
  "residualConcerns": "", "spotCheckPriority": "normal"}
out['Q80'] = d

for i, d in out.items():
    assert d['sourceFile'] == src[i], i
    save(i, d)
print('wrote', sorted(out))
